name: King Tubby
hook: An electronics repairman who rebuilt his own mixing desk and, in doing so, invented the remix.
blurb: Osbourne Ruddock repaired radios and ran a sound system in Kingston. What he did was as much electrical engineering as music. He modified his MCI mixing board, building in his own high-pass filter, so he could drop instruments in and out live and slam echo onto whatever was left, and he played spring reverb and tape delay like instruments rather than using them to fix a sound. Instead of a song with singing, you got a version with the singing mostly gone and the drums, bass and echo enormous. Money drove it: Jamaican sound systems needed music no rival had, and versions on the B-side were a cheap way to get it, so scarcity produced a form. The idea that a finished record is raw material you can rebuild underlies almost all dance music and hip-hop.

signatureTracks.title: Dub From The Roots
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The title track of an album built from his mixes of other producers' rhythms, and the clearest early document of his style.

signatureTracks.title: King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Augustus Pablo's melodica track dismantled and rebuilt as pure space and pressure.
